title: Testing Interchangeability in LLM Agent Teams
one_sentence: Role-matched swaps expose partner-specific coordination costs in memory-equipped LLM dyads.
problem: Does accumulated team experience transfer to an equally experienced replacement?
method: Eight teams per setting in Collab-Overcooked and Hanabi; independent post-formation forks compare intact, placebo, swap, cleared partner notes, amnesia and naive replacement. Swap uncertainty uses four independent pairs.
findings: Swap increased communication per unit progress by 16–63%; the reported recovery trajectory requires numerical clarification.
Partner-note deletion reproduced part of the penalty; longer formation increased partner specificity.
real_contribution: An intervention-based counterexample to broad claims that LLM coordination lacks partner specificity.
biggest_weakness: Few independent pairs; note deletion changes context length; prompted note categories and task-order differences complicate mechanism attribution.
claim_boundary: Supports history-bearing partner compatibility in tested LLM dyads, not mutually acknowledged referential meaning or human–robot generalization.
why_researcher_should_care: Q1 must distinguish partner-model compatibility from jointly accepted meaning, and evaluate coordination cost as well as accuracy.

amsc.master_list_decision: Candidate — Must Read / recovered causal-method counterexample

evidence_notes: Recovered by independent missing-paper attack; outside weekly submission window.
Full HTML sections 3–7 audited; task coupling gradient is observational, not a causal manipulation.

Independent quantitative audit: section 4.4 initial cost ratios 1.15/1.48/1.55 are below Table 1 ten-episode ratios about 1.16/1.51/1.63 despite the stated initial-shock narrative. Aggregation may differ but is unexplained; do not treat the claimed recovery-speed ratio as established.

Reviewer disagreement: missing-paper reviewer recommends Must Read for novelty impact; quantitative reviewer recommends Important for evidentiary limits. Root retains Must Read as reading priority with PRELIMINARY evidence strength.
